Interactive govTable

Source: R/govReactable.R
govReactable.Rd

This function sets table defaults that follow the GOV.UK design system. Some can be changed, such as highlight and borderless. Others are fixed, such as showSortIcon = FALSE, because the default sort icon is not accessible. Each sortable heading is a button, so screen readers announce it and voice control can select it by its visible text. Other arguments for reactable::reactable can be passed in ....

Usage

govReactable(
  df,
  right_col = NULL,
  page_size = 10,
  highlight = TRUE,
  borderless = TRUE,
  min_widths = list(),
  columns = list(),
  caption = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption_size = "l",
  heading_level = 2L,
  caption_id = NULL,
  language = getOption("reactable.language"),
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A dataframe used to generate the table

right_col

A vector of extra column names to right-align. Numeric columns are right-aligned automatically, as GOV.UK guidance says numbers should be right-aligned. Use this for numbers stored as text, such as "£85". To left-align a numeric column, set reactable::colDef(align = "left") for it in columns

page_size

The default number of rows displayed per page (default: 10)

highlight

Highlight table rows on hover

borderless

Remove inner borders from table

min_widths

Customise minimum column width using a list of columns and minimum width in pixels

columns

Change individual columns, for example to set the number of decimal places. Give a named list where each name is a column in df and each value is made with reactable::colDef() (see examples). Columns you leave out keep the GOV.UK defaults, and so does anything you don't set on a column you include. Names that don't match a column are ignored. A headerClass is added to the GOV.UK sort header styling, not swapped for it. Columns with sortable = FALSE show no sort arrow. A custom header on a sortable column goes inside the sort button, so it must not contain links or other interactive content. It must be a string, a tag or an R function. A JS() header on a sortable column is an error. Screen readers name a sortable heading from the column's name, not its header, so if you set a header, set name to the same text, e.g. reactable::colDef(name = "Average cost", header = "Average cost").

caption

Adds a caption heading that screen readers link to the table (using aria-labelledby). Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup. NULL (default) means no caption. For a table built in the server, set the caption on govReactableOutput() instead, as renderGovReactable() gives an error for a captioned table

subtitle

Optional line under the caption, in smaller, lighter text: what the data is, where and when it covers, and the units if every value shares them (e.g. "Cost of bikes (£), England, 2025"). It becomes part of the table's accessible name, with the caption. Needs a caption. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup. NULL (default) shows no subtitle

caption_size

Size of the caption: "s", "m", "l" (default) or "xl". Any other value is an error.

heading_level

The caption's heading level, an integer from 1L to 5L. Defaults to 2L. Use 1L when the table is the main content of the page

caption_id

The id of the caption heading, which the table links to. It must be unique on the page and have no spaces. NULL (default) makes a unique id, so you only need this to link to or style the caption yourself. Setting it without a caption is an error

language

Language options from reactable::reactableLang(), for example to translate the pagination text. Defaults to the reactable.language option. sortLabel is always "{name}" so each heading's accessible name matches its visible text, and setting it gives a warning.

...

Additional arguments passed to reactable::reactable

Value

A reactable widget with GOV.UK classes, or, if caption is given, that widget with a caption heading

Details

Adds a GOV.UK styled table to a Shiny app using reactable. Put it straight into the UI for data that doesn't change, or use renderGovReactable() and govReactableOutput() for data that does. Pass caption to add a heading that screen readers link to the table.

Table titles

Every table needs a title. The Analysis Function guidance on tables suggests two parts, which match two arguments:

  • caption: a short headline stating the message, e.g. "Costs peaked in March".

  • subtitle: what the data is, where and when, e.g. "Cost of bikes, vans and buses (£), England, January to May 2025". Include the units if every value shares them.

A headline is optional. Without one, put the what, where and when in caption and leave out subtitle.

Put the source of the data under the table (for example with gov_text()), not in the title.

Screen reader users hear the caption and subtitle together when they reach the table, so keep them short and don't repeat information. See also the GOV.UK Design System table component.

See also

Other Govstyle tables tabs and accordions: accordion(), govReactable-shiny, govTable(), govTabs(), update_reactable_caption()

Examples

# Tables whose data doesn't change, to put straight into a Shiny app's UI
if (interactive()) {
  # Numeric columns are right-aligned automatically
  govReactable(iris)

  # Use right_col for numbers stored as text, such as "£85"
  govReactable(
    shinyGovstyle::transport_data_small,
    right_col = c("bikes", "cars")
  )

  govReactable(
    iris,
    highlight = FALSE,
    page_size = 5,
    min_widths = list(
      Sepal.Length = 75,
      Sepal.Width = 75,
      Petal.Length = 75,
      Petal.Width = 75
    )
  )

  # Add a caption and subtitle that screen readers link to the table
  govReactable(
    shinyGovstyle::transport_data,
    caption = "Costs peaked in March for every vehicle type",
    subtitle = "Cost of bikes, vans and buses (£), January to May"
  )

  # Show one column to 1 decimal place
  sales_data <- data.frame(
    shop = c("Shop A", "Shop B", "Shop C"),
    growth = c(4, 4.7, 12.34)
  )
  govReactable(
    sales_data,
    columns = list(
      growth = reactable::colDef(
        format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 1)
      )
    )
  )

  # Only `percent` is changed, so `region` and `count` keep the defaults
  count_pct_data <- data.frame(
    region = c("North", "South", "East"),
    count = c(1234, 56, 789),
    percent = c(4, 4.7, 12.34)
  )
  govReactable(
    count_pct_data,
    columns = list(
      percent = reactable::colDef(
        format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 1)
      )
    )
  )
}
